source_text: Diligentiores in orando subiungere in orationibus Alleluia solent et hoc genus psalmos quorum clausulis respondeant qui simul sunt. et est optimum utique institutum omne quod praeponendo et honorando deo conpetit saturatam orationem uelut opimam hostiam admouere.
thought_title: Alleluia and Psalms as the Fitting Close of Prayer
orientation: Tertullian is giving practical instructions for the customs of Christian prayer, and here he commends the practice of adding Alleluia and responsive psalms to prayers.
pass_a_gloss: Those who are more diligent in praying are accustomed to add to their prayers Alleluia and psalms of this kind, to whose closing verses those who are together may respond. And it is certainly the best institution, everything which, by setting before and honoring God, is fitting, to bring near a prayer that has been filled full, as it were a rich victim.

choices.english: Those who are more diligent in praying
choices.why: Keeps the comparative force of diligentiores and the gerund in orando as the sphere of diligence

choices.english: are accustomed to add to their prayers Alleluia
choices.why: Preserves the verb solent as customary practice and subiungere as adding something to the prayers

choices.english: to whose closing verses those who are together may respond
choices.why: Clausulis is rendered as closing verses, and the relative clause keeps the responsive role of those assembled
rejected: to whose conclusions those present respond

choices.term: saturatam orationem uelut opimam hostiam admouere
choices.english: to bring near a prayer that has been filled full, as it were a rich victim
choices.why: Saturatam is rendered as filled full to keep the image of a prayer made complete, and opimam hostiam as rich victim preserves the sacrificial language
rejected: to offer a saturated prayer like a fat sacrifice
to present a full prayer as a sumptuous offering

pass_b_english: Those who are more diligent in praying are accustomed to add Alleluia to their prayers, along with psalms of the kind whose closing verses those assembled may answer. And it is certainly an excellent practice, since everything that serves to set God before us and honor Him is fitting, to bring forward a prayer that has been filled full, like a rich sacrificial offering.

problems.why: 'Victim' in modern English means a sufferer, not a sacrificial offering; the comparison is lost.

fixed: Changed 'victim' to 'offering' because 'victim' in modern English means a sufferer, not a sacrificial offering, and the source 'opimam hostiam' means a rich sacrificial victim/offering.
